narrative:
The model determined that you have a 49% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were the purpose of the loan, the status of your checking account, and the size of the amount you requested. The fact that you are seeking credit for a used car worked in your favor and pulled the prediction toward approval. However, this positive effect was outweighed by two negative influences. Your checking account, which shows a balance between 0 and 200 DM, is relatively uncommon among approved applicants and pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit. Even more important was the loan amount itself: at 7,966 DM it is more than two-and-a-half times the average amount requested by people who were approved. This large sum strongly increased the model's estimate of risk.

Taken together, these factors tipped the balance against you. To improve your chances on a future application, consider requesting a smaller loan amount, waiting until your checking account shows a stronger balance, or exploring other loan purposes that the bank views more favorably. Reviewing your overall credit history and exploring ways to reduce the requested sum could make a meaningful difference next time. (218 words)
